text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — gpuprod-1 saturated, autoscaler failing to increase capacity (scale_limit_reached). Queue length spike in us-east-1. Throttles at 95%. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation. Paging @maria.chen

maria.chen: Oncall here. Seeing alerts, joining. What changed in the last 30m?

ajay.patel: Queue metrics: pending_requests = 6132, active_tokens = 1.2M, throttle_rate = 0.95. Autoscaler logs show repeated "scale_limit_reached" and then "eviction_backpressure".

zoe.rivera: Runtime telemetry — continuous batching throughput dropped ~40% starting at 1755548200. Prefix cache miss rate jumped to 78% at the same time. This maps to a cfg rollout around 1755548000.

ben.keller: Who pushed that rollout? Any config name?

elias.santos: That was me — rolled runtime-batching-config v45 at 1755547989. I changed continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens from 10000 -> 3200 and lowered prefix_cache.prefetch_size to 8 to reduce memory. I did not expect prefix miss rate to blow up. Sorry.

ben.keller: Ok, that explains lower batch sizes -> less throughput -> queue growth. Also prefix_cache smaller -> miss storm -> additional compute work per request -> hotshard eviction thrash.

maria.chen: Immediate mitigations we should do now: 1) rollback runtime-batching-config to v44, 2) manually scale gpuprod-1 to absorb current queue, 3) enable emergency routing to smaller model variants for public customers. I'll execute 2 now.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started: rollback(runtime-batching-config) -> target v44. Job ID: rb-20260315-87. Status: queued.

maria.chen: Running manual scale: `rictl pools scale gpuprod-1 --desired 12 --min 6` (current desired 6).

ajay.patel: Manual scale accepted, initiating provisioning. Note autoscaler has a hard cap for gpuprod-1 at 12 until we sort contracts — pushing to 12 is allowed but 13 would be blocked.

leah.support: CS: Getting reports from two customers with high tail latency (ACME, Nova). ACME: spike in 95p latency from 400ms -> 4.6s, some 503s. Nova: several requests queued >30s. They're flagged for priority outreach.

samir.support: Support logs attached to ACME case: `error=throttle, code=503, model=redwood-medium, attempts=1`. I'll open incident-facing update for them with ETA ~15m.

zoe.rivera: Rollback progress: config rollback in progress across runtime proxies. Once v44 is live we'll expect prefix_cache.prefetch_size to revert and continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens back to 10000. That should raise batching efficiency again.

ben.keller: While rollback completes, reduce eviction aggressiveness to avoid hotshard churn. Suggest: `runtime.kvcache.eviction_rate = 0.5` (was 1.0). Anyone object?

elias.santos: I agree, apply safely. Will patch on a subset first.

deploy-bot: Rollback job rb-20260315-87: in_progress -> 6/9 nodes updated. ETA ~4m.

ajay.patel: New nodes provisioning for gpuprod-1 now maturing, expected ready in ~5m. Watching for spikes in scheduling backlog.

zoe.rivera: Post-rollback telemetry (interim): prefix_cache miss rate falling to 25%, batching avg tokens per batch increasing from 430 -> 2500. Queue length trending down from 6k -> 2.1k.

maria.chen: Good. Apply temporary route-level fallback: route heavy clients to redwood-small model for 60m. `rictl routes update --route heavy_public --fallback redwood-small --duration 60m`

ben.keller: Applied fallback for heavy_public. This should reduce token pressure on gpuprod-1 by approx 30% per load estimate.

leah.support: Sent customer update: we're rolling back a runtime change and scaling capacity; expect improvement in ~10-15m. CS will follow up individually.

samir.support: ACME acknowledged and paused non-critical batch jobs. Nova doing same.

zoe.rivera: Rollback finished: runtime-batching-config v44 active everywhere. Observed: prefix_cache miss -> 12%, batch tokens avg -> 9200, effective throughput nearing pre-incident levels. Queue now 380 and falling. Throttles down to 3%.

ajay.patel: New nodes are healthy and added to pool. Autoscaler still reporting previous limit events — we need to check policy that sets hard caps for autoscale to prevent future manual intervention.

maria.chen: Declaring mitigated. Moving to postmortem. Immediate action items: - Elias to prepare RCA on config regression and add safer rollout guard (feature flag + canary size). - Ajay to audit autoscaler hard caps vs contractual limits and propose buffer policy. - Zoe to add alert for prefix_cache_miss_rate > 30% that triggers config gate. - Ben to document emergency steps used (manual scale + fallback routing). - Leah/Samir to finalize customer comms.

elias.santos: noted. I'll open PR for rollout guard: `canary_percent = 5` + realtime throughput check.

ben.keller: Suggest also rate-limiting config changes on runtime to require two approvers for cache/batching params.

maria.chen: Agreed. I'll kick off the postmortem and set a follow-up meeting. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
__notes: Generated Slack thread for incident about GPU capacity exhaustion due to batching/prefix-cache config regression. Single-string messages, chronological, includes bots and human participants.
